findings.summary: vscode/sessions-view.js refresh() and storeHidden() discard globalState.update promises with `void` and no rejection handler. If the update rejects, the rejection goes unhandled and hide/show-again silently does nothing, which conflicts with the Node rule against floating promises. Catch the rejection and report it, for example with showErrorMessage.

readText returns '' when a read fails, and sessionState then sets lastEventAt to now, so a session whose file is briefly unreadable looks like it has a newer event. pruneHidden in refresh() then deletes its stored entry for good and the card reappears. Before this change the card only flashed back for one refresh. The trigger is unlikely; consider skipping prune or split for sessions that have no parsed events.
The spec scenario says the group reads 'Hidden (1)', but hiddenGroupItem shows the label 'Hidden' with the description '1', as design.md describes. Align the spec text or the label.

sources.content:
# claude-toolkit

Personal Claude Code plugins, laid out as a private plugin marketplace. A proof of concept: it is compatible with the team-shared SDD skill but entirely separate from it, and never changes it. Every toolkit agent carries the `toolkit:` prefix.

## What it does

Two parts, installable separately. **[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) is the setup guide** (written so Claude Code can follow it for you).

1. **Claude sessions**: a "Claude sessions" view with the live, colour-coded status of every Claude session on the machine, a status-bar count, `Ctrl+Alt+N` to jump to waiting sessions, click-to-focus across VS Code windows, a `STATUS:` line at the end of every turn, and optionally a plain Claude tab that opens with a folder ("Toolkit: Open Claude here on startup"). Needs only the extension link and the status hooks.
2. **Coordinator**: open a project and a **coordinator** Claude session starts in an editor tab. It reports the SDD team recap, reads the project board and asks what is next. You tell it the goal; it creates the **worker** sessions the job needs, each in its own named tab with a written brief, and follows them through SendMessage. Workers that still have open work reopen with their conversation the next time you open the project. You can still type in any worker's tab.

| Part | Where |
|---|---|
| Status hooks (session events, `STATUS:` line instruction) and their installer | `status/` |
| `toolkit:coordinator` and `toolkit:worker` agents | `plugins/toolkit/agents/` |
| Start-up hook: runs SDD's team-mailbox pull for the coordinator only | `plugins/toolkit/hooks/` |
| VS Code extension: session view, plain Claude tab, coordinator and worker tabs | `vscode/` |

One project per coordinator; coordinating several projects is planned.

## Coordinator sessions

The extension starts every coordinator and worker session with `--plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit` and `--permission-mode auto` (sessions in the same mode exchange messages without approval prompts). `claude` must be on `PATH`, or set `claudeToolkit.claudePath`; `claudeToolkit.pluginDir` overrides the plugin folder. `claudeToolkit.workerLayout` chooses where worker tabs open: `beside` (default, the column next to the coordinator) or `tabs` (full-width tabs in the coordinator's column).

## Enable a project

Open the project folder and run "Toolkit: Enable coordinator in this folder". It records the folder as enabled on this machine (in the extension's own storage, never in the repository), creates `.coord/`, adds it to `.git/info/exclude` (never `.gitignore`), and opens the coordinator. From then on the coordinator opens whenever VS Code opens the folder; "Toolkit: Start coordinator" opens it again if you closed it. A repository that carries a `.coord/` folder starts nothing until you enable it yourself, and the extension's settings are machine-scoped, so a workspace cannot change which executable or plugin it runs.

### The board (`.coord/`)

| File | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `team.json` | coordinator | `[{ "name", "role", "state": "active" \| "done" }]`; active workers reopen at start-up |
| `workers/<name>/brief.md` | coordinator | the worker's task |
| `workers/<name>/status.md` | worker | `State`, `Summary`, `Next` |
| `requests/<name>.json` | coordinator | `{ "name": "<name>" }`: asks the extension to open the worker; rejected requests leave `<name>.rejected.md` |
| `log.md` | coordinator | decisions, assignments and outcomes |
| `sessions/<session name>.id` | start-up hook | each worker's session ID, so its tab resumes exactly its own conversation, also when the coordinator requests a finished worker again |

Sessions are named `<project>-coordinator` and `<project>-<worker>` (the project folder name in lowercase, other characters as hyphens); tabs show the short name. Enabled projects need different folder names, or their sessions share names.

## Session status

The "Claude sessions" view (its own icon in the Activity Bar, the same in every window; drag it elsewhere once if you prefer) and the status-bar item show every interactive Claude Code session on this machine, toolkit or not. Clicking the status-bar item (`🔔 2 waiting`) shows the session waiting longest; `Ctrl+Alt+N` ("Toolkit: Next waiting session") cycles through the waiting sessions in urgency order; both reach tabs in other windows like a card click does.

| Colour | Status | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| red | waiting for permission / waiting for your answer | `PermissionRequest`; `AskUserQuestion`, or a turn ending with `STATUS: QUESTION` (coordinator and worker) or a final `?` |
| purple | possibly stuck | working with no event for `claudeToolkit.stuckMinutes` (default 10) |
| yellow | finished, needs review | any other end of turn |
| green | working | a prompt or a tool result |
| grey | idle | session started, no prompt yet |

Cards are grouped by project folder (the most urgent project first; each group shows how many of its sessions wait) and sorted by urgency inside each group (longest waiting first) and show the time in that status, the last tool used ("after Bash"; only finished tool calls are recorded) or the tool asking for permission, and the last line of the last message. Click a card to focus its tab, in any VS Code window: each window lists the session tabs it opened in `~/.agent-status/windows/<pid>.json`, and a click on a session held by another window brings that window to the front (by opening its folder) and asks it, through `~/.agent-status/focus/<pid>.json`, to show the tab. A card's tooltip says where its session runs; a session started by hand outside the toolkit's tabs only gets a message. Hide a card with its eye icon until the session's next event; closing a tab hides its card too. Hidden cards are listed in the collapsed "Hidden" group at the bottom of the view, where the eye button shows one again; hiding is remembered across reloads.

The hooks are installed with `node <clone>/status/install.mjs` (see [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)); it backs up `~/.claude/settings.json` first and adds only its own entries, and `--uninstall` removes them. A small synchronous start-up hook (`status/turn-status-hook.mjs`) asks every interactive session to end each turn with `STATUS: QUESTION` or `STATUS: DONE`. "Toolkit: Open Claude here on startup" opens a plain `claude` tab (session `<project>-claude`, no agent, plugin or prompt) whenever the folder opens; "Toolkit: Stop opening Claude here" turns off both the plain tab and the coordinator for the folder.

The event hook (`status/status-hook.mjs`) runs asynchronously, so sessions never wait for it, and appends one line per event to `~/.agent-status/sessions/<session_id>.jsonl`; errors go to `~/.agent-status/hook.log`. It deletes a session's file at `SessionEnd` and leaves a `<session_id>.ended` marker so late background events cannot bring the session back (a new start or resume clears it), and, when a session starts, removes files and markers idle for more than 6 hours (`STALE_HOURS` at the top of the script). Headless sessions (`claude -p`, SDK, SDD's reviewer) are skipped by the observed but undocumented `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-*` value; `tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs` checks it against the installed CLI. A denied permission stays red until the turn ends, because Claude Code fires no event for a denial.

## Plugin delivery

The organization's managed Claude Code policy currently allows only the official Anthropic marketplace, so the plugin is loaded from the clone with `--plugin-dir` (the extension does it; by hand: `claude --plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit`). Update with `git pull`, then reload VS Code.

Once an admin allows the marketplace:

```
claude plugin marketplace add dserri/claude-toolkit
claude plugin install toolkit@claude-toolkit
```

and enable auto-update for `claude-toolkit` in `/plugin` → Marketplaces. The plugin declares no version, so every pushed commit is a release.

## Roll back

Delete the `dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1` junction and reload VS Code; remove a project's `.coord/` folder if you no longer want its board. Sessions started by hand work as before.

## Develop

```
node --test
node --test tests/coordinator.e2e.mjs tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs
```

The first runs the unit, hook, installer and `claude plugin validate` tests (`claude` must be on `PATH`). The second starts real headless sessions with a model call. Tab behaviour and the session view in VS Code are verified by hand.

# Design

## Context

See proposal.md. The view keeps a `hidden` map (session id → latest event time when hidden) in memory; `isVisible` returns a session once it records a newer event.

## Decisions

- **Pure split in `status-core.js`:** `splitHidden(sessions, hidden)` returns `{ visible, hidden }` (hidden newest first) and `pruneHidden(hidden, sessions)` keeps only entries whose session still exists and has no newer event. The view prunes after each read, so storage cannot grow.
- **Storage:** `globalState` key `hiddenSessions` (a plain object), written on hide, show again and prune. Session ids are unique per machine, so global storage is shared correctly between windows.
- **Tree:** root = project groups, then the hidden group (`TreeItemCollapsibleState.Collapsed`, label "Hidden", description = count, `eye-closed` icon). Hidden entries use `contextValue` `hiddenSession`, with the inline command "Show again" (`eye` icon); visible cards keep the hide button. Clicking any entry still focuses its tab.
- **Status bar** counts visible sessions only, as before.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Two windows hide at the same moment] → last write wins; the next refresh in each window reads the stored map.

# Proposal

## Why

Hiding a card (or closing its tab) removes the session from the view with no way back until it records a new event, so a mistaken click loses track of a chat. Hidden state also lives only in memory, so a window reload brings back every card the developer hid or closed.

## What Changes

- Hidden and closed sessions move to a "Hidden" group at the bottom of the view, collapsed by default, with a count; each entry has a button that shows it again.
- Hidden state is stored per machine, so reloads keep it; entries of sessions that no longer exist are dropped.
- A hidden session still returns by itself when it records a new event.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `session-status`: the hidden group, restoring a session, persistent hiding.

## Impact

`vscode/status-core.js`, `vscode/sessions-view.js`, `vscode/package.json`, tests, README.

# Spec Delta

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Hidden group

Sessions hidden by the developer or by closing their tab SHALL be listed in a "Hidden" group after all project groups, collapsed by default, labelled with their count and ordered by latest event first, and SHALL NOT count in the status-bar waiting count. Each entry SHALL offer "Show again", which returns the session to its project group. The group SHALL not appear when nothing is hidden.

#### Scenario: Mistaken hide

- **WHEN** the developer hides a card by mistake
- **THEN** it appears in the collapsed "Hidden (1)" group, and "Show again" puts it back in its project group

#### Scenario: Closed tab

- **WHEN** the developer closes a session's tab
- **THEN** its card leaves the project group and is listed only in the collapsed hidden group

#### Scenario: New activity

- **WHEN** a hidden session records a new event
- **THEN** it returns to its project group by itself

### Requirement: Persistent hiding

Hidden sessions SHALL be stored in the extension's storage on this machine, so a window reload keeps them hidden; entries of sessions that no longer have a session file, or that recorded a newer event, SHALL be dropped.

#### Scenario: Reload

- **WHEN** the developer hides a card and reloads the window
- **THEN** the card stays in the hidden group

# Tasks

## 1. Implementation

- [x] 1.1 Add `splitHidden` and `pruneHidden` to `vscode/status-core.js` with tests
- [x] 1.2 Persist the hidden map, add the hidden group and "Show again" in `sessions-view.js`/`package.json`; verify VS Code loads it
- [x] 1.3 Document the hidden group in README

## 2. Acceptance

- [x] 2.1 With the developer: hide a card, find it in the collapsed group, show it again; close a tab and find it there; reload and see hidden cards stay hidden
